speaker: Patient
text: 69-year-old male. The patient presents with pain in his left great toe, hips, and knees that worsens with activity and improves with rest. He reports that the symptoms have progressively gotten worse over the past several years.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. The pattern of pain worsening with activity and improving with rest in the hips and knees is typical of osteoarthritis, but the involvement of the left great toe raises suspicion for gout or psoriatic arthritis. Has the left great toe ever become red, hot, and swollen suddenly, and do you have a history of kidney stones or alcohol consumption? REQUEST TEST: Uric_Acid, RF, HLA-B27

speaker: Doctor
text: The uric acid, rheumatoid factor, and HLA-B27 results are all normal, which makes gout, rheumatoid arthritis, and ankylosing spondylitis unlikely. Given your age and the specific location of pain in the left great toe alongside your hip and knee symptoms, is there any history of psoriasis, nail pitting, or a family history of psoriatic arthritis? speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of obesity, smoking, and hypertension, along with pain worsening with activity, osteoarthritis is highly probable.
